To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the more social overload a user of social network sites experiences, the less satisfied he or she is with his/her use of the site and the more likely he or she is to quit using the social network site.

social overload leads to emotional exhaustion and that this emotional exhaustion in turn leads to a decreased user satisfaction and an increased intention to discontinue the usage of social networking sites.
social overload is a relevant stressor for social network sites' users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why users of social network site report feelings of being emotionally exhausted.
the fact that social network sites, which originally intend to provide hedonistic value to users, are currently perceived by users as a stressor.
the question how to prevent users from being emotionally exhausted, while using social networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress-strain model is an appropriate framework for explaining the negative effects of social networking on the users' satisfaction and their discontinuous usage intention.
social overload is a stressor that causes emotional exhaustion, which in turn leads to decreased satisfaction with the use of Facebook.
social network sites are not only a tool for hedonic purposes, but also for stress reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social overload is a stressor, that induces feelings of being emotionally exhausted, and leads users to be dissatisfied, which in the end leads users to quit the usage of social network sites.
the social overload of using Facebook is a stressor, which causes emotional exhaustion and leads to dissatisfaction with Facebook and a discontinuous usage intention.
social overload is an important antecedent to explain the negative effects of social network sites on their users' well-being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social overload is a stressor that leads to feelings of being emotionally exhausted.
it is important to consider the hedonic value of social network sites as well as the negative aspects of using these sites.
it is not the use of social network sites itself that leads to negative outcomes but rather the feeling of being overwhelmed by the use.
